misconception.text: Magnetic field lines can cross each other.

correction.text: They never cross. The field at a point has one direction, and two field lines through the same point would mean two directions at once.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: A current in a wire has no magnetic field around it.

correction.text: It has one, in circles around the wire, with the direction set by the right hand rule.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

stem.text: A particle moving parallel to a uniform magnetic field experiences

options.text: a force perpendicular to the field

explanation.text: The force is $qvB\sin\theta$, and with the velocity along the field the angle is zero, so the force is zero. The field changes only the direction of the particle's path.

stem.text: Ampere's law relates the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor to

explanation.text: Ampere's law says the circulation of the magnetic field around the conductor is proportional to the current enclosed.

stem.text: Two long parallel wires carrying currents in the same direction

options.text: have no effect on each other
attract only if the currents are unequal

explanation.text: Same-direction currents repel, and opposite-direction currents attract.
